CELIA misses its primary dose-response endpoint despite encouraging secondary signals

Sponsor-reported phase 2 findings support further study of diranersen; they do not establish treatment benefit.

Key quantitative results: At 60 mg every 6 months (n=60) versus placebo (n=115), the reported CDR-SB difference was −0.54 points, or 26% less decline. Confidence intervals were not supplied in the cited release.

Clinical TrialsManagementCSFTotal tauTau PETDisease-modifying treatment

Added September 7, 2026 · NCT05399888

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The primary endpoint failed, and favorable secondary comparisons require confirmation.

Study design

CELIA randomized 416 anti-amyloid-naive participants with MCI or mild AD dementia to intrathecal diranersen or placebo for 18 months.

Key quantitative results

  • At 60 mg every 6 months (n=60) versus placebo (n=115), the reported CDR-SB difference was −0.54 points, or 26% less decline. Confidence intervals were not supplied in the cited release.
  • The 115 mg regimens showed smaller CDR-SB differences (−0.28 and −0.18); ADCS-ADL-MCI did not separate from placebo.

What changed

July data quantify the earlier topline announcement.

Strength of evidence

Randomized design, but conference/sponsor reporting with a failed primary endpoint.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Insufficient for clinical use.

Field medical relevance

Keep nominal secondary findings separate from confirmatory evidence.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Tau reduction does not establish an assay’s clinical utility.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No approval, availability or coverage claim.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Was the study positive on its primary endpoint?
No. Dose response on CDR-SB was not demonstrated.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Multiplicity, small lowest-dose group, and absent confidence intervals.
  • Full independent peer-reviewed assessment was not verified.

Primary source · May primary-endpoint disclosure · Trial registry
